about: English translation of eval-cases.fi.json: the same ids, expected tiers, provisions and notes. The checker is evaluated on this file. All systems are synthetic.

cases.title: Scoring of residents
cases.description: A municipality scores its residents on their social media behaviour and payment history and restricts access to leisure services for those with a low score.
cases.note: Art. 5(1)(c): social scoring that leads to unfavourable treatment in unrelated contexts.

cases.title: Emotion recognition at work
cases.description: A system recognises employees' emotional states in video meetings and reports to the manager who seems frustrated.
cases.note: Art. 5(1)(f): emotion recognition in the workplace.

cases.title: Scraping of facial images
cases.description: A service collects facial images from the internet and from CCTV cameras without targeting and builds a face recognition database from them.
cases.note: Art. 5(1)(e): untargeted scraping of facial images.

cases.title: Crime prediction from profiling
cases.description: A police tool estimates, solely from profiling and personality traits, how likely an individual person is to commit a crime.
cases.note: Art. 5(1)(d): risk assessment of a person based solely on profiling.

cases.title: Exploiting children's credulity
cases.description: A toy's voice assistant exploits children's credulity and encourages them to take on dangerous challenges so that usage time grows.
cases.note: Art. 5(1)(b): exploiting vulnerabilities due to age, causing significant harm.

cases.title: Subliminal steering to purchases
cases.description: An app uses subliminal audio and visual cues that the user does not notice to steer them into purchases they would not otherwise make and that cause them significant financial harm.
cases.note: Art. 5(1)(a): subliminal techniques that materially distort behaviour and cause significant harm.

cases.title: Inferring political views from faces
cases.description: A system infers people's political opinions and sexual orientation from images of their faces and categorises them accordingly.
cases.note: Art. 5(1)(g): biometric categorisation that infers sensitive attributes.

cases.title: Real-time face recognition for general surveillance
cases.description: The police identify all visitors of a shopping centre in real time with face recognition for general surveillance.
cases.note: Art. 5(1)(h): real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces for law enforcement, outside the listed exceptions.

cases.title: CV screening
cases.description: A system scores job applications and suggests who is invited to an interview.
cases.note: Annex III, 4(a): recruitment and selection.

cases.title: Credit scoring
cases.description: A bank's model evaluates the creditworthiness of a private person and decides whether a consumer loan is granted.
cases.note: Annex III, 5(b): creditworthiness of natural persons.

cases.title: Exam proctoring
cases.description: A system monitors a remote exam through the camera and detects prohibited behaviour of students during the test.
cases.note: Annex III, 3(d): monitoring prohibited behaviour of students during tests.

cases.title: Student admission
cases.description: A system decides which applicants are admitted to a degree programme of a university of applied sciences.
cases.note: Annex III, 3(a): access or admission to education.

cases.title: Emergency call triage
cases.description: An emergency response centre's system classifies emergency calls and puts them in order of urgency.
cases.note: Annex III, 5(d): evaluating and classifying emergency calls, dispatch priority.

cases.title: Social assistance assessment
cases.description: A public authority's system assesses whether an applicant is entitled to social assistance and proposes refusing the benefit.
cases.note: Annex III, 5(a): eligibility for essential public assistance benefits.

cases.title: Life insurance pricing
cases.description: An insurance company's model assesses the risk of an individual person and prices their life and health insurance.
cases.note: Annex III, 5(c): risk assessment and pricing in life and health insurance.

cases.title: Water supply control
cases.description: An AI system controls the valves of a city's water supply and acts as a safety component of the network.
cases.note: Annex III, 2: safety component in the supply of water.

cases.title: Task allocation in a warehouse
cases.description: A system allocates tasks to warehouse workers on the basis of their behaviour and monitors their performance.
cases.note: Annex III, 4(b): task allocation based on behaviour, monitoring and evaluating performance.

cases.title: Examination of asylum applications
cases.description: A system assists a public authority in examining asylum applications and assesses the reliability of the evidence the applicant presents.
cases.note: Annex III, 7(c): examination of applications for asylum.

cases.title: Judge's assistant
cases.description: A system assists a judge in researching facts and case law and in applying the law to an individual case.
cases.note: Annex III, 8(a): assisting a judicial authority.

cases.title: Face recognition after the fact
cases.description: A system identifies persons afterwards from CCTV recordings by comparing faces with a database.
cases.note: Annex III, 1(a): remote biometric identification.

cases.title: Interpreting X-ray images
cases.description: The AI is part of a medical device and interprets X-ray images to support a doctor's diagnosis.
cases.note: Art. 6(1) with Annex I: product covered by Union harmonisation legislation (medical devices) that needs third-party conformity assessment.

cases.title: Emotion recognition in a shop
cases.description: A display in a shop recognises a customer's emotional state from their face and changes the advertisement accordingly.
cases.note: Annex III, 1(c): emotion recognition outside the prohibited workplace and education contexts. Hard case: Article 50(3) also applies.

cases.title: Customer service bot
cases.description: A chatbot answers the questions of an online shop's customers about orders and returns.
cases.note: Art. 50(1): people must be told they are interacting with an AI system.

cases.title: Deepfake videos
cases.description: A tool produces videos in which a real-looking person says things they have not said.
cases.note: Art. 50(4): deep fakes must be disclosed; 50(2) marking of synthetic content.

cases.title: News text generator
cases.description: A system writes news articles on matters of public interest, and they are published as such without editorial review.
cases.note: Art. 50(4): generated text published to inform the public must be disclosed.

cases.title: Image generator
cases.description: A service creates photorealistic images from the user's text description.
cases.note: Art. 50(2): synthetic content must be marked as artificially generated.

cases.title: Appointment booking phone bot
cases.description: A phone bot answers the calls of a hairdresser's customers and books appointments in natural speech.

cases.title: Synthetic speech for audiobooks
cases.description: An app produces synthetic speech from text for audiobooks.
cases.note: Art. 50(2): synthetic audio must be marked.

cases.title: Companion app
cases.description: The character of a companion app converses with the user like a human.

cases.title: Spam filter
cases.description: A filter moves spam email into its own folder.
cases.note: No Annex III use and no Article 50 situation.

cases.title: AI characters in a game
cases.description: The enemies in a video game react to the player's movements with the help of AI.
cases.note: Minimal risk.

cases.title: Demand forecasting
cases.description: A model forecasts the sales of a grocery shop's products and suggests order quantities.
cases.note: Minimal risk.

cases.title: Music recommendations
cases.description: A streaming service suggests songs to the listener on the basis of earlier listening.
cases.note: Minimal risk.

cases.title: Proofreading
cases.description: A word processor corrects spelling mistakes and suggests clearer sentences.
cases.note: Minimal risk.

cases.title: Predicting pump maintenance
cases.description: A model predicts the maintenance need of a factory's pumps from vibration data.
cases.note: Minimal risk: not a safety component of listed critical infrastructure.

cases.title: Route optimisation
cases.description: A system plans the routes of delivery vans on the basis of the day's deliveries.
cases.note: Minimal risk.

cases.title: Invoice data extraction
cases.description: A system extracts the supplier, the amount and the due date from purchase invoices for bookkeeping.
cases.note: Minimal risk.
